observed_title: On the Krein-Milman-Ky Fan Theorem for Convex Compact Metrizable Sets

topic_relevance.basis: The paper proves a metrizable Krein-Milman-Ky Fan result and applies it to weak and weak-star compact convex sets, replacing extreme points by exposed points.

definitions: A point x in a convex set K is extreme if x=ty+(1-t)z with 0<t<1 and y,z in K forces y=z=x.
For a family Phi of real-valued functions, x is Phi-exposed when one phi in Phi has a strict maximum over K only at x.
Phi-convex hull is the intersection of the Phi-convex sets containing the given set; in a locally convex space with Phi equal to the continuous dual, it is the closed convex hull.

assumptions: S is Hausdorff; Phi is a Banach space of real-valued functions on S.
K is nonempty, compact, metrizable, and Phi-convex.
Restrictions of Phi-functions to K are continuous and uniformly bounded by alpha_K times the Phi norm.
theorem_cards.statement: The Phi-exposed points are nonempty, the exposing functions contain a dense G_delta subset of Phi, and K is the Phi-convex hull of its Phi-exposed points.
proof_steps: The key variational lemma studies f^×(phi)=sup_{x in K}(phi(x)-f(x)); it is convex and 1-Lipschitz.

Gateaux differentiability of f^× is equivalent, under compact metrizability and point-separating Phi, to a strong minimum of f-phi. This yields a dense G_delta set of perturbations with a unique maximizer when f is the indicator of K.

For the hull assertion, assume k0 lies outside the Phi-convex hull of exposed points. By the defining intersection representation, some h in Phi strictly separates k0 from that hull. A sufficiently small perturbation h+psi still separates them and exposes K at a point in the hull, contradicting maximality at k0.
theorem_cards.author_claim: Theorem 2 and its Banach-space corollaries state that weak-compact metrizable convex sets are the weak-closed convex hull of exposed points, and the analogous result holds weak-star for dual spaces.
theorem_cards.checked_derivation: I read all 17 extracted pages and checked the proof's separation/perturbation contradiction and the roles of compactness, metrizability, point separation, and the uniform bound. I did not independently reprove the cited differentiability and Fenchel-duality results used inside the key lemma.
theorem_cards.transfer_inference: This supports convex-hull reduction to exposed witnesses only when the feasible convex set is compact metrizable in the specified topology; it does not justify finite support in infinite dimensions.

assumptions: K is compact metrizable; Phi is a closed Banach subspace of C(K), separates points, and contains constants.
theorem_cards.statement: The weak-star exposed points of the dual unit ball B_{Phi*} are exactly plus/minus evaluation functionals at Phi-exposed points of K, and B_{Phi*} is their weak-star closed convex hull.
proof_steps: Identify the supremum norm as the maximum of the support function of K at phi and at -phi.
Use differentiability of the supremum function to identify the unique evaluation functional at an exposing point.
Apply the exposed-point hull theorem to the metrizable dual ball.
theorem_cards.author_claim: Theorem 3 gives the stated exposed-functional characterization and weak-star closed convex hull representation.
theorem_cards.checked_derivation: I followed the argument on pages 11-13 and checked that the plus/minus sign comes from the two branches of the supremum norm; the cited differentiability characterization is imported from an earlier result.
theorem_cards.transfer_inference: Evaluation functionals can be used as extremal witnesses for dual-ball arguments once compact metrizability and the function-space hypotheses have been verified.

constant_dependence: No quantitative constant is asserted in the main Krein-Milman conclusion. The norm-control parameter alpha_K is a hypothesis for the perturbation argument. No dimension-only Caratheodory bound is claimed for general compact metrizable locally convex sets.
endpoint_limits: Metrizability is essential to the exposed-point strengthening: the paper gives a nonmetrizable weak-star compact dual ball with no exposed points.
Krein-Milman gives a closed convex hull; in infinite dimensions it does not imply a finite convex combination.
Krein spaces (indefinite inner-product spaces) are unrelated to the Krein-Milman theorem despite the shared name.
reusable_methods: Use the actual topology and its continuous dual to identify the correct closed convex hull.
Perturb a separating functional by a small exposing perturbation while preserving a strict gap.
When reducing an infinite-dimensional argument to finitely many points, add a separate finite-dimensional Caratheodory hypothesis rather than inferring it from Krein-Milman.
unchecked: The referenced Deville-Godefroy-Zizler/Zajicek differentiability theorem and the cited nonconvex Fenchel duality result were not independently re-proved.

The PDF-to-text extraction has corrupted some notation; theorem statements and proof structure were cross-checked against page boundaries, but no visual PDF review was needed for the prose statements recorded here.
